guards.title: Escape closes the address dialog and returns focus
guards.goal: Escape dismisses the dialog and focus returns to the trigger

plan.root_cause: The focus trap's delayInitialFocus option defaults to true, deferring initial focus until after the current event loop, so the assertion checking focus immediately after opening the dialog fails.
plan.repair_strategy: Disable the delayInitialFocus option when activating the trap so that initial focus occurs synchronously with dialog opening.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users will now receive immediate focus on the first focusable element (street input) when the dialog opens, satisfying WCAG 2.4.3 (focus order) and 2.1.1 (keyboard).
functional_risks: Changing the timing of focus initialization could affect scenarios that rely on the delayed focus (e.g., if the dialog content is not yet ready). In this case the dialog is static and ready immediately, so risk is low.
verification_requirements: After activating the dialog, focus must be on #street input.
Pressing Enter after entering an address must save the address and update the status.
Pressing Escape must close the dialog and return focus to the #open button.
The speed fieldset must remain disabled until an address is saved.

plan.root_cause: The focus trap's delayInitialFocus option defaults to true, deferring initial focus until after the current event loop. When the dialog opens via Enter key, the assertion checking immediate focus on #street fails because focus hasn't moved yet.
plan.repair_strategy: Pass { delayInitialFocus: false } to trap.activate() so initial focus occurs synchronously with dialog opening, matching the exact original source formatting.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users will now receive immediate focus on the first focusable element (street input) when the dialog opens, satisfying WCAG 2.4.3 (focus order) and 2.1.1 (keyboard).
functional_risks: Changing the timing of focus initialization could affect scenarios that rely on the delayed focus (e.g., if the dialog content is not yet ready). In this case the dialog is static and ready immediately, so risk is low.

plan.root_cause: The focus trap's delayInitialFocus option defaults to true, deferring initial focus until after the current event loop. When the dialog opens via Enter key on the #open button, the assertion checking immediate focus on #street fails because focus hasn't moved yet. The original code only handles the click event, but the keyboard test triggers a keydown event that may be checked before the click handler runs.
plan.repair_strategy: Pass { delayInitialFocus: false } to trap.activate() in both the click and keydown handlers for the #open button, ensuring immediate synchronous focus on the first focusable element (#street) when the dialog opens.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users will now receive immediate focus on the first focusable element (street input) when the dialog opens via Enter key or click, satisfying WCAG 2.4.3 (focus order) and 2.1.1 (keyboard).
functional_risks: Adding a keydown handler duplicates the activation logic, but the trap's activate method returns early if already active, so no double-activation occurs.

Changing the timing of focus initialization could affect scenarios that rely on the delayed focus (e.g., if the dialog content is not yet ready). In this case the dialog is static and ready immediately, so risk is low.
verification_requirements: After activating the dialog via Enter key, focus must be on #street input.
Pressing Enter after entering an address must save the address and update the status.
Pressing Escape must close the dialog and return focus to the #open button.
The speed fieldset must remain disabled until an address is saved.
